analysis.title: Financial Conditions Tightening But Not Tight
key_insights: The FOMC kept rates unchanged on 28 Oct 2026 in a 10-2 vote. The statement upgraded its description of the expansion from solid to strong.
TS Lombard's own assessment suggests wage growth may already be bottoming, even though the statement points to job gains running in parallel with supply.

Chair Warsh's press conference said financial conditions are tightening for some businesses but are not tight overall. TS Lombard agrees: higher yields in H2 are imposing some discipline in the AI space, but there is no evidence in the real or financial economy that conditions are tight.
TS Lombard says most of its expected quarterly Fed hike trajectory is now priced in. Hotter core inflation and stable-to-reaccelerating job markets support a hawkish view.

TS Lombard argues the Fed is likely comfortable with current rate pricing and wants to stop the market from extrapolating to a hike at every meeting. Hiking on 28 Oct would have reduced the Fed's optionality.

An increasing number of FOMC members are coming around to the idea that more is needed to tame inflation. The debate over how much tightening is required depends on data, especially evidence of sustained re-acceleration in job markets.
TS Lombard says a September hike was a test of Fed independence because of the SEP, bond market pressure and the greater distance from the midterms. With the hike delivered, market urgency has faded.
TS Lombard argues a gradual Fed can be a more hawkish Fed. Consensus has re-settled on the view that the Fed will not go far, and the firm thinks it may be wrong again.

A more gradual hiking cycle would have less impact on sentiment than the fast pace of 2022-23 and give the economy more time to adjust. This could imply a higher terminal rate than consensus assumes, if the AI boom does not materialise.

macro_indicators.reading: Unchanged at the 28 Oct 2026 FOMC meeting, 10-2 vote
macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held after hiking in September. TS Lombard reads the hold as keeping optionality, not as the end of tightening.

macro_indicators.reading: TS Lombard expects a higher terminal rate than consensus pencils in, if the AI boom does not materialise
macro_indicators.interpretation: A gradual hiking cycle with a higher end point than the market expects.

macro_indicators.reading: Quarterly hikes, most of which TS Lombard says is now priced in
macro_indicators.interpretation: The market has largely caught up to TS Lombard's hawkish call, which limits further repricing unless data re-accelerate.

risk_factors: Re-acceleration in job markets would push the Fed to tighten more than the current pricing implies.
The AI boom failing to materialise is the condition under which TS Lombard sees a higher terminal rate.
Consensus has been wrong on the Fed twice: it did not expect the September hike, and it may be underestimating how far the Fed goes.
Fed independence and midterm politics were a factor in the September meeting.
cross_bank_references: The Street consensus said the Fed could not hike, then overcorrected after September (TS Lombard's characterisation of the sell-side).
TS Lombard refers to an earlier note published the day before (27 Oct) explaining why consensus on the Fed's terminal path may be wrong.

key_data_points.metric: FOMC vote to hold rates unchanged

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish view: hotter core inflation, stable-to-reaccelerating jobs and a gradual hiking cycle point to a higher terminal rate than consensus assumes, with a hike possible at coming meetings.
tension_points.bear_case: Consensus view: even if the Fed raises rates it will not go far. Sell-side voices complained that the Fed did not hike on 28 Oct.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Job-market data failing to show sustained re-acceleration would undercut the case for more tightening, and a materialising AI boom would remove the case for a higher terminal rate.

theme_stances.key_argument: A gradual Fed can be a more hawkish Fed, and the terminal rate may be higher than consensus pencils in.
theme_stances.evidence: a gradual Fed can be a more hawkish Fed

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher yields in H2 are imposing some discipline in the AI space, but there is no evidence in the real or financial economy that conditions are tight.
theme_stances.evidence: there is not evidence in the real or financial economy that financial conditions are tight
